description.narrative:
Insatsen avser ett kärnstöd till organisationen PEN International om totalt 36 MSEK under en fyraårsperiod 2020-2023. För denna period har PEN utvecklat en strategi, med fokus på fyra tematiska områden:
1) Skapa nya utrymmen för litteratur, språk, debatt, dialog, idéer och åsikter. 2) Förbättra situationen för utsatta skribenter på flykt, som är fängslade eller på annat sätt förföljda. 3) Påverka strukturella hot och barriärer mot yttrandefrihet. 4) Stärka den institutionella kapaciteten och hållbarheten hos PEN som organisation.
Total budget för perioden är cirka 94 MSEK. Sidas stöd uppgår till 36 MSEK.

PEN International is a global network consisting of more than 20 000 writers, affiliated with over 150 federated centres in more than 100 countries. The overall goal of the organisation is to promote and defend freedom of expression, literatures, linguistic diversity and mutual respect and tolerace across borders.
PEN:s strategic plan for 2020-2023 has four thematic domains: 1) Creating new spaces for literature, language, debate, dialogue ideas and opinions. 2) Improving the situation of writers at risk who are displaced, imprisoned or otherwise persecuted. 3) Addressing structural threats and barriers to freedom of expression. 4) Strengthening the institutional capacity and sustainability of PEN, so that the movement is fully representative and relevant.
The total budget for the four-year period is around 94 MSEK. Sidas contribution for this period amounts to 36 MSEK.

PEN International has adopted a new strategy for the years 2024-2028. The intended global outcomes are slightly changed with a clearer focus on human rights and advocacy. The document is also shorter. Sida assesses that the new strategy has an even stronger foundation in HRBA than the previous one. The outcomes are:
Outcome 1: Creating spaces for literature, language, debates, dialogue, ideas and opinions.
Outcome 2: Strengthening human rights policy and practice.
Outcome 3: Improvement in the situation of writers at risk who are imprisoned or otherwise persecuted.
Outcome 4: Strengthen the institutional capacity, standing and sustainability of PEN Centres, so that the movement is an effective champion of free expression for all.

description.narrative:
Among the results PEN reports during 2023 are: - In 2023/24 Pen International had 122 documented cases of persecuted writers on its Case Lise. PEN International continues the monitoring and researching of violations of freedom of expression across the world. - In Europe and Central Asia, PEN issued 63 statements and calls to action on key cases, provided nine emergency grants and drafted two asylum support letters. - On the situation in Cuba, Pen International launched the report "Metodo Cuba" in collaboration with other CSO's. The report has been used by Inter-American Commission on Human Rights as well as the Universal Periodic Review. - In October, PEN International in collaboration with PEN centers, issued the report "Toxic narratives". This report was discussed with representatives for UN, UNESCO and OSCE, and contributed to the inclusion of writers in policy measures for journalists at risk in Bosnia and Herzegovina. - The work with PEN Centers contributes to and creates synergies with the advocacy work and support to artists at risk. - PEN International has continued its work with PEN Centers through the Civil Society Programme in the global south. The work on "the invisible child" has reached schools in Mexico (Chiapas), Malawi, Sierra Leone, Zimbabwe, South Africa (Afrikaans) and Togo, with topics on marginalized children and girls situations. PEN has also held a regional CSP capacity building workshop in Manilla with participation of nine PEN centers.
PEN International, as one of the worlds oldest human rights organisations, continues to play a key role when it comes to defending freedom of speech, literature, language rights and protection of writers and artists. It is a solidarity movement with a broad base of grass root organisations in the PEN centers, as well as an impactful actor in the public debate and normative agenda.
Right now, as far as Sida can assess, PEN International is the only civil society organisation which works on a global mandate with protection of writers, poets and artists, and one of few that works with advocacy within the UN system on the issue of Artistic freedom and the rights of artists. There are other organisations that works regionally and locally with the same issues, but there is a need for a strong global organisation to gather the voices, and here PEN fills an important role.
